critical_correction.what_was_wrong: neupert_fit built the lagged SXR series by zero-padding its first `lag` samples, then scored the correlation over the FULL window mask instead of the lag-aware mask. Every candidate lag was therefore correlated partly against padding zeros.
critical_correction.effect: Inflated the integral-model r and biased the winning lag.
critical_correction.note: The 4/4 INTEGRAL verdict is unchanged; only the magnitude and lead time moved slightly.

neupert.band_policy: Same band for every event. Auto-selection previously picked 80-150 keV for 2024-05-11 and 40-60 keV for the others, which makes cross-event comparison invalid.
neupert.statistical_caveat: n=4. The smallest two-sided sign-test p attainable when all 4 events agree is 0.125, so no result in this set can reach p<0.05. Wording must be 'consistent with' / 'exploratory', never 'demonstrates' or 'proves'.

figure_generator_divergence.issue: paper/generate_figures.py reimplements the Neupert chain instead of importing scripts/neupert_analysis.py, so it omits channel_quality/MIN_CHANNEL_STD health screening and the zero-inflation refusal gate.
figure_generator_divergence.resolution: Unify on scripts/neupert_analysis.py before publication. The direct-model r differs most, so the discrepancy is in HXR channel screening, not in the lag logic.

ml_fixed_threshold.verdict: WORSE than a constant base-rate forecast (BSS < 0). ~90% of alarms are false.

ml_tuned_threshold.note: This run is the origin of the manuscript's 'TSS 0.32 / tuned threshold 0.32' claim, which was never computed by any script.

ml_baselines.caveat: Both baselines score 0 because at theta=0.45 they never predict positive. The 'beats baselines' flag is vacuous and must not be cited as evidence of skill.

blocking_integrity_findings.detail: metrics.py computes TSS = POD - POFD (Peirce score). Bloomfield et al. 2012, the cited benchmark, define TSS = HTR - FAR. On one illustrative matrix the same counts give +0.32 under one convention and -0.63 under the other.
blocking_integrity_findings.required_action: Either report both conventions, or restate TSS as HTR - FAR so the Bloomfield comparison is valid.

literature_grounding.status: SXR-follows-integral-HXR is established physics since 1969. This project re-verifies it instrument-side and must never be framed as a discovery.
literature_grounding.sample_adequacy: n=4 supports 'consistent with the Neupert effect', not 'demonstrates' it.

metric_convention_correction.previous_claim: Manuscript and evaluator asserted Bloomfield et al. 2012 define TSS as HTR-FAR and that our POD-POFD values were therefore NOT comparable.
metric_convention_correction.verified_fact: Bloomfield et al. 2012 (ApJ 747, L41) adopt the Hanssen-Kuipers discriminant, TSS = (ad-bc)/[(a+c)(b+d)], which is algebraically identical to POD - POFD (Peirce score). It is recommended there precisely because it is invariant to the event/no-event sample ratio.
metric_convention_correction.impact: No change to any measured number. The comparison is now stated correctly, and the paper notes the absolute skill is far below the published 24-h optima (TSS 0.46 for >=C1.0, 0.74 for X-class).
metric_convention_correction.residual_caution: Some papers use the label TSS loosely for HTR-FAR; those values are not comparable. Woodcock 1976 is now cited for the metric definition.
